newsitem.title: FRANCE: Car bomb kills two, wounds 28 in Algeria.
newsitem.headline: Car bomb kills two, wounds 28 in Algeria.

text.p: A car bomb exploded in southern Algiers on Thursday killing two people and wounding 28, eyewitnesses and residents said on Friday.
The booby-trapped car went off in the centre of Baraki, a southern Algiers district, targeting a local security guard station, witnesses said by telephone from Algiers.
The government set up an 16,000 strong force known as Communal Guards, drawn from civilian anti-Islamist volunteers, in early 1995 to back security forces and army troops fighting Moslem rebels.
"Most of the casualties were among passers-by," one witness said. The identity of the two people killed in the attack was not immediately known. There was no official word about the bombing.

No one claimed responsibility for the attack which occurred two days ahead of a crucial national conference to adopt Algerian President Liamine Zeroual's reforms plan in a bid to pull the country out of nearly five years of civil strife.
The authorities blame Moslem guerrillas for a series of bomb attacks over the past four years.
Government-appointed human rights watchdog, Human Rights National Observatory (ONDH), said in August that about 1,400 civilans had been killed by Moslem guerrilla bombs in the past two years.

An estimated 50,000 people have died in Algeria's violence pitting Moslem rebels against government forces since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
Algeria's leadership and about 1,000 politicians are to gather on Saturday to chart a new future for the crisis-ridden nation in a "National Conference of Understanding" on Saturday and Sunday.
Main opposition parties are staying away and the outlawed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) is barred from the meeting.

The FIS warned this week that those taking part "would have to take entire responsibility for the consequences...of the aggravation of the crisis with its accompanying destruction, misery and poverty."
